title: Rigveda 4.46: To Vayu or Indra and Vayu
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.46: To Vayu or Indra and Vayu: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.46 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Vayu or Indra and Vayu. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 307r-307v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 4.46.1-4 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 7, varga 22); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 307r
translation.original_text:
1agra̍m pibā̱ madhū̍nāṁ su̱taṁ vā̍yo̱ divi̍ṣṭiṣu | tvaṁ hi pū̍rva̱pā asi̍ ||
2śa̱tenā̍ no a̱bhiṣṭi̍bhir ni̱yutvā̱m̐ indra̍sārathiḥ | vāyo̍ su̱tasya̍ tṛmpatam ||
3ā vā̍ṁ sa̱hasra̱ṁ hara̍ya̱ indra̍vāyū a̱bhi praya̍ḥ | vaha̍ntu̱ soma̍pītaye ||
4ratha̱ṁ hira̍ṇyavandhura̱m indra̍vāyū svadhva̱ram | ā hi sthātho̍ divi̱spṛśa̍m ||
translation.text:
1DRINK the best draught of Soma-juice, O Vâyu, at our holy rites: For thou art he who drinketh first.
2Come, team-drawn, with thy hundred helps, with Indra, seated in the car, Vaya, and drink your fill of juice.
3May steeds a thousand bring you both, Indra. and Vâyu, hitherward To drink the Soma, to the feagt.
4For ye, O Indra-Vâyu, mount the goldenseated car that aids The sacrifice, that reaches heaven.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 307r (numbered 116r by the scribe) (OPenn image 307, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.45.6 ‹cit aśvān yuyujānaḥ īyate›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 307v (numbered 116v by the scribe), begins in RV 4.46.5 ‹-indravāyūiti iha ā gatam›. Verses 4.46.1-4 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1agram | piba | madhūnām | sutam | vayo iti | diviṣṭiṣu | tvam | hi | pūrva-pāḥ | asi
2śatena | naḥ | abhiṣṭi-bhiḥ | niyutvān | indra-sārathiḥ | vāyo iti | sutasya | tṛmpatam
3ā | vām | sahasram | harayaḥ | indravāyūiti | abhi | prayaḥ | vahantu | soma-pītaye
4ratham | hiraṇya-vandhuram | indravāyūiti | su-adhvaram | ā | hi | sthāthaḥ | div i-spṛśam

translation.original_ref: RV 4.46.5-7 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 7, varga 22); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 307v
translation.original_text:
5rathe̍na pṛthu̱pāja̍sā dā̱śvāṁsa̱m upa̍ gacchatam | indra̍vāyū i̱hā ga̍tam ||
6indra̍vāyū a̱yaṁ su̱tas taṁ de̱vebhi̍ḥ sa̱joṣa̍sā | piba̍taṁ dā̱śuṣo̍ gṛ̱he ||
7i̱ha pra̱yāṇa̍m astu vā̱m indra̍vāyū vi̱moca̍nam | i̱ha vā̱ṁ soma̍pītaye ||
translation.text:
5On far-refulgent chariot come unto the man who offers gifts: Come, Indra-Vâyu, hitherward.
6Here, Indra-Vâyu, is the juice: drink it, accordant with the Gods, Within the giver's dwelling-place.
7Hither, O Indra-Vâyu, be your journey here unyoke your steeds, Here for your draught of Soma juice.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 307v (numbered 116v by the scribe) (OPenn image 308, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.46.5 ‹-indravāyūiti iha ā gatam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 308r (numbered 117r by the scribe), begins in RV 4.47.4 ‹yajña-vāhasā indravāyūiti ni yacchatam›. Verses 4.46.5-7 end on this page; 4.46.5 begins on fol. 307r (numbered 116r by the scribe).
translation.edition_text:
5rathena | pṛthu-pājasā | dāśvāṃsam | upa | gacchatam | indravāyūiti | iha | ā | gatam
6indravāyūiti | ayam | sutaḥ | tam | devebhiḥ | sa-joṣasā | pibatam | dāśuṣaḥ | gṛhe
7iha | pra-yānam | astu | vām | indravāyūiti | vi-mocanam | iha | vām | soma-pītaye
